title: Diagonal language time bound
statement: Let $g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be time-constructible. The language of binary strings $x$ for which the diagonal simulator does not halt with output $1$ after exactly $g(|x|)$ steps is decidable by a Turing machine within time $c\bigl(g(n)+1\bigr)$ on inputs of length $n$, for some constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$.
replaced:
Let $g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be time-constructible. The language of words $x$ for
which the diagonal simulation does not halt at time $g(|x|)$ with output the single bit
$1$ is decidable in time $c\bigl(g(n)+1\bigr)$ for some constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$.
